activity.notes: Yeshe-Ö was a historical ruler of Guge and a major patron of the later dissemination of Buddhism. His regnal chronology is materially inconsistent across later Tibetan and modern reconstructions. A critical biography on Tibetan Law states that he took monastic vows in 989 and handed over kingship to Khor re. ATLAS therefore records only c.989 as a representative final-ruler point instead of fabricating a full reign interval from conflicting chronologies.

sources.title: Biography of Lha Lama Yeshe Ö — Tibetan Law
sources.citation_text: The critical biography states that Yeshe Ö belonged to Guge's ruling family, united a wider area, and took monastic vows in 989 while handing over the kingship to Khor re.

sources.title: Lha Lama Yeshe Wo — The Treasury of Lives
sources.citation_text: The peer-reviewed Treasury of Lives biography identifies Yeshe Wo/Yeshe Ö as a historical tenth- to eleventh-century Tibetan figure associated with Guge and Tholing.
